profile.campus: New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio (Meta's New Albany data center campus)
profile.address: Beech Road Southwest, New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, 43062
profile.reading: This building (OSM-tagged "NAO 1/NAO 2") is part of Meta's New Albany data center campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio, just east of Columbus. Meta broke ground on the site in 2017 and, per its own fact sheet, has invested more than $1.5 billion in the campus, employs 300-plus people once complete, drew 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, and has provided more than $5.6 million in direct funding to Franklin- and Licking County-area schools and nonprofits, alongside its usual LEED Gold, net-zero, and water-positive-by-2030 commitments. Real-estate and land-acquisition reporting sourced from county deed records shows Meta, operating through its Sidecat LLC affiliate, has assembled 1,345 acres across 18 parcels in Licking County since an initial 1.3-acre purchase in October 2017, with $679 million spent on land alone; a 2025 round of purchases covering 514 acres cost $566 million, pushing per-acre land prices above $1.1 million as the campus expanded aggressively. AEP Ohio has said it is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings describe a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction directly on the campus, targeting completion in 2026, so Meta can power part of the expansion independently of the regional grid. Local and regional reporting (Spectrum News 1, News 5 Cleveland) describes the expanded campus as a "gigawatt-scale" data center, with an Ohio State University sustainability researcher estimating its electricity draw at roughly the equivalent of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers, and construction employing thousands of workers across the region even though permanent staffing is comparatively small relative to the facility's power draw. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact building count, or per-building square footage for individual New Albany structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

profile.regional_context: Licking County's New Albany area has become, per News 5 Cleveland, one of the starting points of Ohio's broader data center boom, with Microsoft and Google facilities also sited nearby and Cologix separately reported to be planning a large Licking County campus of its own. Community advocacy groups such as Stop Ohio Data Centers have organized around concerns over the sector's land use, water use, and grid impact in the New Albany/Licking County corridor, while state and AEP Ohio utility filings document the scale of dedicated transmission and generation infrastructure being built to serve Meta's campus specifically.

reading.body:
Meta's New Albany campus in Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio sits on 1,345 acres assembled at a cost of $679 million, with $566 million spent in a single 2025 land-acquisition round that pushed per-acre prices above $1.1 million. The operator describes the expanded campus as gigawatt-scale, and a regional estimate equates its electricity draw to the consumption of 800,000 to 900,000 homes, several times larger than other regional data centers. Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity, exact square footage, or confirmed building count for New Albany, so the translated scale of compute hosted here cannot be stated from published operator data.

The campus is backed by dedicated grid infrastructure: AEP Ohio is building two 13-mile, 345-kilovolt transmission lines specifically to serve the site, and state utility filings document a 200-megawatt natural gas plant approved for construction on campus, targeting 2026 completion to supply part of the facility independent of the regional grid. This degree of dedicated transmission and on-site generation is material evidence that New Albany is positioned to draw power at a scale that requires grid reinforcement designed for this single customer.

New Albany has anchored Ohio's data center expansion and is now one of three major hyperscaler campuses in Licking County alongside Microsoft and Google facilities nearby, with Cologix also reported to be planning a large campus in the county. Ohio's 76 mapped data center facilities include only eight with published capacity figures totaling 60.4 megawatts, so New Albany's gigawatt-scale power draw makes it one of the state's most significant capacity nodes even without operator publication of specific IT load figures.
